subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@knoxhealth.com>, Amit Shah <amit@knoxhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Hi Priya / Amit,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

1) Key pain points you described
- Rising per-token costs + unpredictable spikes when embeddings/batch workloads run.
- Hard rate-limit and backoff behavior impacting customer-facing flows.
- Lack of control over data residency and encryption-at-rest for some workloads.
- Limited auditability (request-level logs and KV cache visibility) for compliance and incident response.

2) Current stack / usage patterns
- Text generation: primarily OpenAI (gpt-4/4o for higher-quality assistants, gpt-3.5 for lighter workloads).
- Safety/guardrails: Anthropic used for some classification/safety checks.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for semantic search (index size ~50M vectors).
- Orchestration: homegrown router that pins model providers by route; some retry logic.

3) Success criteria for a migration / PoC
- Maintain or improve generation quality (human eval pass-rate within ~5% of current).
- Reduce per-token inference cost by ~30-50% depending on workload.
- Keep 95th percentile latency for interactive routes <= 300ms (target).
- Meet security/compliance needs: KMS integration, per-request audit logs, and regional controls (US/EU).

4) Compatibility needs we discussed
- API parity for streaming completions + function/tool-calling (important for your assistant flows).
- Embeddings format/compat to avoid reindexing pipeline if possible (or a low-cost reindex path).
- Safety-classifier parity for content filtering; ability to route to Anthropic-like classifiers or run custom models.

5) Model shortlist (initial candidates)
- Llama 3 (instruct variants) — for higher-quality instruction-following.
- Mistral 7B / Mistral Instruct — cost-effective for many generation tasks.
- Falcon / Open weights (40B instruct) — checkpoint for accuracy tests.
- Cohere/Mosaic style embeddings models (Mosaic or Open-embedding families) — to evaluate embedding parity and cost.

6) Immediate next steps
- Redwood: share the migration playbook and our security pack (attached). This includes a compatibility checklist and recommended quantization/throughput profiles. [Attachment: migration-playbook.xlsx], [Attachment: redwood-security-pack.pdf]
- Knox: share a representative set of prompts, 2-3 benchmark conversations, and a subset (~5k) of embedding vectors (sample) we can use for quality / perf testing.
- Schedule technical deep-dive (SE call) week of 2026-06-17 to go over API mapping, function-calling parity, and a PoC plan.
- Commercial touchpoint: Aditya will follow up with proposed pricing for Dedicated/Private options and a pilot commitment model.

Proposed time for the SE deep-dive: Thu 2026-06-17 10:00am PT — does that work for your team?

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0162
[Attachment: redwood-security-pack.pdf] [Attachment: migration-playbook.xlsx]

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple of clarifications and asks from our side:

- Confirmed shortlist: happy to start with Llama 3 and Mistral as primary candidates; would like Falcon as a fallback for large-context tests.
- Compliance: our security team requires explicit KMS/HSM support and proof of per-request audit logs for the pilot. Can you confirm Redwood supports customer KMS and request-level logging in the Private/Dedicated offering?
- Embeddings: we want to avoid a full reindex if possible. If you can show a migration path that supports the same vector dims and transforms or a low-cost reindex plan, that will be a big win.
- For the PoC dataset: we can export a 5k-sample of our indexing vectors and send by EOD Monday (we’ll share a secure Drive link).

Thu 6/17 10am PT works for the SE deep-dive. Please include Rishi (technical SE) and our infra lead (Amit).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of AI Engineering | Knox Health
priya@knoxhealth.com
